summary: Moffitt Butte, Klamath County: the only dated record is 1940, when the Walker Range Patrol held the lookout in emergency status. Nothing else is documented.

events.note: Held in emergency status by the Walker Range Patrol, with telephone contact to LaPine

evidence.supports: only dated entry, 1940; emergency status with telephone to LaPine
evidence.quote: 1940: The lookout was held in emergency status by the Walker Range Patrol with telephone communications with LaPine.

evidence.supports: Summit Butte carries the same township and range code, 24S-11E
evidence.quote: Walker Range Patrol / Private Timber Company ; 24S-11E-35

evidence.supports: Walker Range Patrol staffed Summit Butte 110 days in 1940; reports by telephone to LaPine
evidence.quote: 1940: The lookout was staffed by the Walker Range Patrol for 110 days. The reporting station was at LaPine and linked by telephone.

notes_for_editor: One dated entry (1940) on the Forest Lookouts page; no build date, design or fate found in two searches. The story is below the usual 120-word floor because the evidence is that thin. County check: the Forest Lookouts page files the butte under Klamath County, but a Deschutes National Forest map label seen in a search snippet (not read) places Moffitt Butte near La Pine and Crescent. Confirm the county before publishing. The Summit Butte page is used only for the shared township and range code and the patrol's 1940 season.
